purpose: Prevent the locked recovery comparison from being over-interpreted as an equal-realized-FPR sensitivity comparison when the selected statistic and frozen single-epoch comparator use independently calibrated thresholds.

scientific_issue.problem: Independent envelope calibration does not guarantee equal realized false-alarm rates on the locked null panel. A recovery difference can therefore reflect both method sensitivity and operating-point differences.
scientific_issue.implication: The primary recovery delta is a comparison of two method-plus-calibration systems at independently calibrated operating points. It must not be described as a pure equal-FPR sensitivity gain unless the locked null evidence supports that characterization.

interpretation_rules: Always report selected and comparator locked-null false-alarm counts and rates by regime alongside the recovery comparison.
Describe the primary recovery delta as a comparison at independently calibrated operating points.
Do not claim equal-FPR sensitivity unless the realized locked-null evidence supports that statement.

If the comparator is more conservative on locked null data, explicitly state that some recovery difference may be attributable to operating-point conservatism rather than the leave-one-out statistic alone.

If the comparator exceeds the study's 1 percent point-FPR level in any locked null regime, do not describe the comparator as satisfying the selected method's safety gate; preserve the protocol-defined recovery comparison without retroactive threshold changes.
Report every regime and every diagnostic regardless of whether it favors the selected statistic or comparator.
